questions: Is a NodeExecution a value identified by all of its facts, or an entity minted for the attempt and identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)` or by a separate identifier?
Is a NodeExecution a content-substitutable value or an issued entity identified by its run, node, map index and attempt number?
Is NodeExecution an occurrence entity identified by its run/node/element/attempt coordinates, or a substitutable content value?

quotes:
### Identity

value

### Identity evidence

Substitution: an attempt's record is issued once. Continuity: none; a further
attempt is a further record.

Substitution: fails — an execution is an observation; two runs of the same pair
are two observations with equal facts possible, and both are kept, so the
record is told apart by its minted `trial_execution_id` (A01 rule 2), not by its
values. Continuity: trivial; it is issued once and never changed. Entity issued
once, not a value (SPEC_STANDARD 15.1.1: a value has no identifier of its own;
pre-contract data closure, 2026-10-03).
judgement.why: The change did not touch either identity passage or make NodeExecution identity newly consequential.

topics.topic: AdmissionVerdict reuse versus recreation on identical resubmission
questions: When the same implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created from the newly run TrialExecutions?
When an equal implementation is submitted again against the same corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict observation created with new TrialExecutions?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about repeated admission against an unchanged corpus.

precedent.topic: Whether repeated admission against an unchanged corpus reuses or creates an AdmissionVerdict and TrialExecutions
quotes: Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.
precedent.why: The later rule says the existing verdict is reused, so no new admission TrialExecutions are created for an unchanged implementation-and-corpus pair.

topics.topic: ProofResult identity across changing binding state
questions: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can have different results as binding state changes?
What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can produce different results as binding state changes?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about ProofResult identity as a referenced binding changes state.

precedent.topic: How ProofResult identity accounts for changing referenced-binding status
quotes: Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result. Continuity: none.
precedent.why: The change did not touch M17 or make ProofResult identity newly consequential.

topics.topic: Actor provenance for automatic admission and activation
questions: When an agent resubmits an existing implementation, which model records the agent whose current request caused the new admission executions and activation, rather than the implementation's original submitter?
Must a read-only flow activation retain the owner or agent whose request caused the kernel's automatic activation, and if so, where is that actor recorded?

topics.topic: Effect of trial-corpus changes on existing activations and run pinning
questions: When adding or capturing a trial case changes the corpus, what happens to an existing activation whose admission covered the previous corpus, and may new runs still pin it?

topics.topic: Guard evaluation semantics for edges from mapped nodes
questions: May a guarded edge originate from a mapped node, and if so is its guard evaluated separately for each mapped element or once against the collected output?

topics.topic: Installation identity and mutable configuration semantics
questions: Does a configuration change create a new Installation identity, or mutate/revise the configuration of the same installation, and which configuration fields besides tokens can change without restart?

topics.topic: Mapping primary actions to MCP operations and activation availability
questions: Which primary actions are distinct MCP operations, which are variants of the listed operations, and may agents invoke activation for proven read-only versions through that surface?

topics.topic: Product action and returned data for implementation inspection and repair
questions: Which product action lets an agent enter the repair view and read an implementation body, and what does ordinary function inspection return?

topics.topic: Terminal run behavior for outstanding executions and effects
questions: What happens to already-running node executions and already-sent `in_flight` effects when another action makes the run `cancelled` or `refused`, including whether their later responses may update NodeExecution and EffectAttempt records?
